answer: Behavioral Terrain Fingerprinting. Each identity accumulates a sparse feature vector from its interaction graph; a random-walk kernel smooths these vectors and clusters them into overlapping terrain regions. Sybil clusters appear as improbable density ridges, like a karst formation, flagged when cross-region bridge edges exceed a calibrated null. Enforcement quarantines flagged clusters retroactively, withholding accrued rewards. An attacker must sustain distinct behavioral signatures across regions, raising the per-identity operating cost roughly tenfold.
